Rashi on Ketubot 13b:11:1.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה וכו' - לרבי יהושע פריך: נהי נמי דאין אפוטרופוס לעריות, תיפוק ליה דלא דמי לשבויה, דהתם רוב פסולין כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:11:1.english: And let [the tanna] derive [it], etc. - [The Gemara] raises an objection against Rabbi Yehoshua: Even though there is no guardian against forbidden sexual relations, let it derive [the distinction] that [this case] is not comparable to a captive woman, for there the majority [of men] are unfit, etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:11:2.hebrew: מכשיר אפי' ברוב פסולים - דאמרינן אוקמה אחזקה. ועל רוב פסולים שהיו מכשירים אותה, הביא הוא להם ראיה מן השבויה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:11:2.english: He deems [her] fit even in [a case of] a majority of unfit [men] - For we say, "Establish her on her presumptive status [of fitness]." And regarding [a case of] a majority of unfit [men] where they would deem her fit, he [Rabbi Yehoshua] brought them a proof from the captive woman.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:13:1.hebrew: אית לה חזקה דכשרות - וי"ל אשה זו בחזקת כשרות עומדת, ומספק אתה בא לפוסלה — אל תפסילנה מספק:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:13:1.english: She has a presumptive status of fitness - And one can say: this woman stands in a presumptive status of fitness, and out of doubt you come to disqualify her — do not disqualify her out of doubt.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:14:1.hebrew: לא שתוקי וכשר - כלומר, שתוקי הוא במקצת, שאם כהן היה הבועל והעובר יהיה זכר, משתקין אותו מדין כהונה כדלקמן. אבל כשר הוא ליוחסין, שאם נקבה היא תינשא לכהונה, ואם זכר הוא בתו ואלמנתו כשרות לכהונה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:14:1.english: No, a shetuki, and fit - That is to say, [the child] is a shetuki in part, in that if the one who had intercourse [with the mother] was a priest and the fetus is a male, we silence him from the law of the priesthood, as [explained] below. However, [the child] is fit with respect to lineage, so that if it is a female, she may marry into the priesthood, and if it is a male, his daughter and his widow are fit for the priesthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:15:1.english: And one of them separated - and it is not known which one he is.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:15:2.hebrew: הולד שתוקי - ואע"פ שברור לנו שמכהן כשר בא, והאי שתוקי על כרחך כשר ליוחסין, ואם נקבה היא — ראויה לכהן, וקרי ליה שתוקי:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:15:2.english: The child is a shetuki - Even though it is clear to us that he comes from a fit priest — and this shetuki is perforce fit for lineage, and if it is a female, she is fit [to marry] a priest — yet [Shmuel] calls him a shetuki.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:16:1.english: From the status of priesthood - That he may not perform [the Temple] service and may not eat terumah.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:16:2.english: Attributed to him - That we know who his father is.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:1:1.hebrew: לחורבה - סתמא לבעילה, שהוא מקום לזנות:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:1:1.english: Into a ruin - Ordinarily, [it is] for intercourse, for it is a place for promiscuity.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:3:1.hebrew: חורבה דמתא - סתם בעילתה מאחד מבני העיר, ואיכא למימר בעיר שרובה ישראל כשרים קאמר:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:3:1.english: A ruin in the city - Ordinarily, her intercourse [was] with one of the residents of the city, and one can say [that it] is speaking of a city whose majority are fit Israelites.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:3:2.hebrew: דדברא - ספק אחד מסוף העולם בא לכאן, ורוב העולם עובדי כוכבים הם, ופוסלים אשה בביאתם לכהונה, כדאמר ביבמות (דף מה.) ובקדושין (דף עה:): יצאו עובד כוכבים ועבד, שאין לו אלמנות וגירושין בה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:3:2.english: Of the field - [There is] a doubt [whether] someone from the end of the world came here, and the majority of the world are idolaters, and they disqualify a woman from [marrying into] the priesthood through their intercourse, as it says in Yevamot (45a) and in Kiddushin (75b): "An idolater and a slave are excluded, for he has no [halakhic] widowhood or divorce with her."

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:5:1.english: This is testimony that a woman - [she] herself is fit to say, "I had intercourse with a fit [man]."

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:5:2.english: She is not deemed credible - to marry a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:6:1.hebrew: אמרו לו אבל - הן, כמו אבל שרה אשתך (בראשית י״ז:י״ט), דמתרגמינן בקושטא:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:6:1.english: They said to him: Aval - [This means] "yes," like "Aval [Indeed], Sarah your wife" (Genesis 17:19), which we translate [into Aramaic as] "bekushta" [truly].

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:6:2.hebrew: ומה הפרש בין זו לזו - ר' יהושע קאמר לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:6:2.english: And what difference [is there] between this [woman] and that [woman] - Rabbi Yehoshua says this.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:6:3.hebrew: לזו יש עדים - שנבעלה, דכיון דנשבית לבין העובדי כוכבים והם פרוצים בעריות, כולנו עדים שנבעלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:6:3.english: For this [woman] there are witnesses - [Meaning] that she engaged in intercourse; for since she was taken captive among the idolaters and they are licentious with regard to forbidden sexual relations, we are all witnesses that she engaged in intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:6:4.hebrew: ולזו אין עדים - שנבעלה, שלא ראוה אלא מדברת. ומיגו דאי בעיא אמרה לא נבעלתי, כי אמרה נמי לכשר נבעלתי, מהימנא:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:6:4.english: And for this one there are no witnesses - that she engaged in intercourse, for they only saw her speaking [with him]. And since if she wanted she could have said, "I did not engage in intercourse," even when she says, "I engaged in intercourse with a fit [man]," she is believed.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:7:1.hebrew: אף לזו - כלומר, אף כאן יש אחת שיש לה עדים, ואתם חולקים עלי בהיותה מעוברת:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:7:1.english: Even for this [woman] - That is to say, here too there is one who has witnesses, and you disagree with me when she is pregnant.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:7:2.english: They said to him, etc. - Later on, [the Gemara] explains what they were answering him [in response] to what he said to them.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:7:3.english: There is no steward, etc. - [The Gemara] explains [this] later.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:8:1.hebrew: בד"א - דנאמנת לר"ג:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:8:1.english: In what [case] are [these] statements said - That she is believed according to Rabban Gamliel.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:8:2.hebrew: בעדות אשה בגופה - כלומר, להכשיר את עצמה לכהונה, דלא מחזקינן לה בנבעלה לפסול:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:8:2.english: In [the case of] the testimony of a woman regarding herself - That is to say, to render herself fit for the priesthood, as we do not presume her to have had relations with an unfit [man].

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:9:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר להו כו' - כלומר, מאי קאמר להו איהו דקא מהדרי ליה אינהו "רוב עובדי כוכבים פרוצים בעריות"? כלום תשובה היא זו על מה שאמר להם "אף לזו יש לה עדים"? אין לך פרוץ גדול מזה, דקחזינן דנתעברה ממנו:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:9:1.english: What did he say to them, etc. - That is to say, what did he say to them that they replied to him, "Most idolaters are steeped in sexual immorality"? Is this any answer to what he said to them, "This one too has witnesses"? There is no greater [proof of] immorality than this, since we see that she became pregnant from him.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:9:2.english: You answered us concerning the pregnant woman - [With] a complete and decisive answer.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:9:3.hebrew: מדברת היינו שבויה - מה מדברת אין לה עדים, אף שבויה אין לה עדים בבעילה, ואתם מחזיקים אותה כנבעלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13b:9:3.english: [The case of a woman] speaking is the same as [the case of] a captive - Just as [the woman] speaking has no witnesses, so too a captive has no witnesses regarding intercourse, and [yet] you treat her as one who has had intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:9:4.english: Steeped in sexual immorality - And this [woman] certainly had intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 13b:9:5.english: There is no steward for sexual immorality - You cannot be a steward for her to say, "She did not have intercourse."

Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:11:1.hebrew: מסייע ליה לר' יהושע בן לוי - הקשה ר"ת: אכתי תיפוק ליה דהתם בשבויה כל פסולים, והכא בחורבה דדברא רוב. ותירץ דרוב ככל, וליכא למימר: במדברת דליכא אלא רוב איכא למימר סמוך מיעוטא לחזקה ואיתרע לה רובא — דאפילו אית להו סמוך מיעוטא לחזקה לר"ג ור' יהושע, מ"מ לא הוי אלא פלגא ופלגא, ודין הוא שתאסר מספק, דספק איסורא לחומרא. ולא דמי לתינוק שנמצא בצד העיסה בפרק עשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף פ. ושם) דמטהרין מטעם סמוך מיעוטא לחזקה, דאם אמרו ספק טומאה לטהר, יאמרו ספק איסור להתיר, כדאמרינן פרק כיסוי הדם (חולין דף פו:):
Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:11:1.english: [This] supports Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi - Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: Still, let [the distinction] be derived [from the fact] that there, in the case of a captive woman, all [the men] are unfit, whereas here, in [the case of] a ruin in the field, [only] a majority [are unfit]. And he answered that a majority is like the entirety. And one cannot say [that] in [the case of] a woman who spoke [with a man], where there is only a majority [of unfit men], one can say "combine the minority [of fit men] with [her] presumptive status [of fitness], and the majority is weakened" — because even if Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua hold [the principle of] "combine the minority with the presumptive status," nevertheless it is only half and half, and by law she should be forbidden out of doubt, for a doubt regarding a prohibition is [ruled] stringently. And it is not comparable to [the case of] a child found beside dough in the chapter Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 80a and ibid.), where they declare [it] pure on the grounds of "combine the minority with the presumptive status," for [there it is a matter of ritual purity, and we say:] "If they said [that] a doubt regarding ritual impurity is [ruled] pure, shall they say [that] a doubt regarding a prohibition is [ruled] permitted?" — as we say in the chapter Kisui Hadam (Chullin 86b).

Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:11:2.hebrew: מכשיר אפילו ברוב פסולים - והא דקאמרינן בפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין עד. ושם) גבי "אבא שאול היה קורא לשתוקי בדוקי", ומפרש בגמרא שבודקין אמו ואומרת "לכשר נבעלתי", ופריך: כמאן? כר"ג? תנינא חדא זימנא: "היתה מעוברת כו'" — פי': והוה ליה למתני "וכן אמר אבא שאול", וכן פי' שם בקונטרס — ומשני: דאבא שאול עדיפא מר"ג, דאי מהתם הוה אמינא: ברוב כשרים אצלה כו' — אע"ג דאמרי' הכא דר"ג מכשיר אפילו ברוב פסולין, אבא שאול קאי אמתני', וממתני' לא משמע מידי דאיירי ברוב פסולים. והא דפריך התם לעיל למאי דהוה בעי למימר דאבא שאול אתא להכשיר בבתה: "הניחא למ"ד: לדברי המכשיר בה פוסל בבתה, אבל למ"ד מכשיר בבתה, מאי איכא למימר?" — התם פריך שפיר, דאפי' לזעירי לשון המשנה דקתני "מה טיבו של עובר זה" משמע דאתא להכשיר בבתה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:11:2.english: He deems her fit even where the majority are unfit - And [regarding] that which we say in the chapter Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 74a and there[abouts]) concerning "Abba Shaul used to call a shetuki a beduki," and the Gemara explains that we examine his mother and she says, "I had relations with a fit man," and [the Gemara] asks: "Like whom? Like Rabban Gamliel? We have [already] learned it once: 'She was pregnant, etc.'" — meaning: it should have taught "and so said Abba Shaul," and so Rashi explained there — and [the Gemara] answers: "[The ruling] of Abba Shaul is stronger than [that of] Rabban Gamliel, for if [we derived it only] from there, I would have said: where the majority are fit for her, etc." — even though we say here that Rabban Gamliel deems her fit even where the majority are unfit, Abba Shaul is referring to the Mishnah, and from the Mishnah it is not implied at all that it is dealing with a majority of unfit [men]. And as for what [the Gemara] asks there earlier, according to what it wanted to say that Abba Shaul came to deem [her] fit with respect to her daughter: "This works well according to the one who says: according to the statement of the one who deems her fit, he deems her daughter unfit; but according to the one who says he deems her daughter fit, what is there to say?" — there it asks well, for even according to Ze'iri, the wording of the Mishnah, which teaches "What is the nature of this fetus?", implies that it comes to deem [her] fit with respect to her daughter.

Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:16:1.hebrew: פשיטא מי ידעינן אבוה מנו - הכא לא בעי לשנויי: "לא צריכא דאי תפס", כדמשני בפרק עשרה יוחסין (קידושין דף עה. ושם) גבי ארוסה שעיברה — דהתם רגלים לדבר דמארוס נתעברה, ואיכא למיתלי ביה טפי מבאיניש דעלמא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:16:1.english: "It is obvious; do we know who his father is?" - Here, [the Gemara] did not want to answer, "It is only necessary [to teach this] for [the case] where he seized [the property]," as it answers in the chapter [entitled] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 75a and there) regarding a betrothed woman who became pregnant — for there, there are grounds [to assume] that she became pregnant by the betrothed man, and it is more reasonable to attribute [the pregnancy] to him than to any other person.

Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:16:2.hebrew: בעינן זרעו מיוחס אחריו - והא דאמר בהחולץ (יבמות דף לז.): "ראשון ראוי להיות כ"ג" גבי ספק בן תשע לראשון, בפרק נושאין על האנוסה (יבמות דף ק:) פריך לה, ומשני: זרעו מיוחס אחריו דרבנן, וקרא אסמכתא בעלמא הוא; וכי גזור רבנן — בזנות, בנישואין לא גזור:
Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:16:2.english: We require [that] "his offspring are attributed to him" - And [regarding] that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] HaCholetz (Yevamot 37a): "The first [son] is fit to be a High Priest," regarding a doubtful nine-month [child] of the first [husband] — in the chapter Nose'in Al HaAnusah (Yevamot 100b), [the Gemara] raises this difficulty and answers: [The requirement that] "his offspring are attributed to him" is rabbinic, and the verse is merely a scriptural support (asmakhta); and when the Rabbis decreed [this disqualification], [it was] in [a case of] licentiousness, [whereas] in [a case of] marriage they did not decree [it].

Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:17:1.hebrew: [ההוא ארוס וארוסתו - והא דאמר בעשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף עה.): "איתמר, הבא על ארוסתו בבית חמיו, רב אמר: הולד ממזר, ושמואל אמר: הולד שתוקי" — כשלא בדקו את אמו, דאי בשבדקו, קשיא דשמואל אדשמואל! דהכא אמר שמואל דנאמנת, דהלכה כרבן גמליאל דנאמנת, והתם קאמר: "איפוך, שמואל אמר הולד ממזר"! וכן משמע דבמסקנא משני התם: "לעולם לא תיפוך כו'", ומפרש: "מאי שתוקי? שבודקין את אמו ואומרת: לכשר נבעלתי". ואם תאמר: אכתי לשמואל דהתם משמע דוקא בבא על ארוסתו בבית חמיו מהני בדיקה, והכא משמע אפילו כי לא מודה אמר שמואל דנאמנת כרבן גמליאל? ויש לומר, דהא דנקט "בא", היינו משום רבותא דרב נקטיה, דאפילו הכי אמר הולד ממזר. אי נמי, התם הוא דבעינן "בא", משום דאיירי בדדיימא מעלמא, כדאמר רבא ביבמות בשלהי אלמנה לכהן גדול: "מסתברא מילתא דרב בדדיימא מעלמא", והכא בדלא דיימא מעלמא מיירי. ועוד, דבכל הספרים גרס בקדושין: "ארוסה שעיברה", וההיא דוקא קאמר שבודקין, אבל בבא א"צ בדיקה. ומיהו קשה ללישנא קמא ביבמות בסוף פ' אלמנה, דפליגי רב ושמואל בבא, ומסיק התם אביי דאע"ג דלא דיימא מעלמא פליגי, דדלמא מדאפקרה נפשה לגבי ארוס מפקרה נפשה לגבי עלמא — הא אמר הכא "חדא דקא מודה", ומשמע דכשר אפילו לר' יהושע, ו"בא" כמודה דמי, דהא מודה דהכא אינו אלא שהיה אומר שבא עליה, דפשיטא שלא היה מזנב אחריה לאורבה שלא תזנה! ובין לרב ובין לשמואל אסור הוא בבת ישראל, דשתוקי דקאמר לשמואל היינו דאסור בבת ישראל לכולהו לישני דבפרק בתרא דקדושין; וללישנא דבדוקי נמי קשה טפי, דמשמע דאפילו ע"י בדיקת האם לא מיתכשר אלא לר"ג, אבל לרבי יהושע לא, והכא אמר "דהא קא מודה" וכשר לכ"ע! ושמא יש לחלק, ד"בא" דהתם היינו שפעם אחת בא עליה, אבל מודה דהכא דקאמר "מיניה", היינו שבא עליה ביאות הרבה והיה רגיל אצלה תמיד, וכדאמרינן: רוב בעילות הלך אחר הבעל:
Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:17:1.english: [A certain betrothed man and his betrothed - And that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 75a): "It was stated: If one has relations with his betrothed in her father-in-law's house, Rav says: The child is a mamzer, and Shmuel says: The child is a shetuki" — [this refers to a case] where they did not examine his mother; for if [it referred to a case] where they did examine [her], Shmuel would contradict Shmuel! For here Shmuel says that she is believed, since the halakha is in accordance with Rabban Gamliel that she is believed, whereas there [in Kiddushin] he says: "Reverse [the opinions]: Shmuel says the child is a mamzer"! And so too it is implied, since in the conclusion there [the Gemara] answers: "Actually, do not reverse, etc.," and explains: "What is a shetuki? That they examine his mother, and she says: 'I had relations with a fit man.'" And if you say: Still, according to Shmuel there, it is implied that specifically when one has relations with his betrothed in her father-in-law's house is the examination effective, whereas here it is implied that even when he does not admit [it], Shmuel says she is believed like Rabban Gamliel? One can answer that the reason [the Gemara] stated "one who has relations" is because of the novelty of Rav's [ruling] that it stated it, for even so [Rav] says the child is a mamzer. Alternatively, it is specifically there that we require "one who has relations," because it is dealing with [a woman] who has a bad reputation from the public, as Rava says in Yevamot at the end of [the chapter] Almanah LeKohen Gadol: "Rav's statement makes sense where she has a bad reputation from the public," whereas here it is dealing with [a woman] who does not have a bad reputation from the public. And furthermore, in all the texts, the reading in Kiddushin is "a betrothed woman who became pregnant," and regarding that [case] specifically does [the Gemara] say that they examine [her], whereas where he had relations [with her], no examination is needed. However, it is difficult according to the first version in Yevamot at the end of the chapter Almanah [LeKohen Gadol], where Rav and Shmuel disagree about [a case where] he had relations [with her], and Abaye concludes there that even though she does not have a bad reputation from the public they disagree, because perhaps since she made herself available to [her] betrothed, she [also] made herself available to the public — [yet] behold, [Rav Yosef] says here: "First, he admits [it]," which implies that [the child] is fit even according to Rabbi Yehoshua, and "one who had relations" is comparable to "one who admits," for "admitting" here is nothing other than his saying that he had relations with her, since it is obvious that he was not tailing after her to lie in wait for her so that she would not act promiscuously! Yet [in Yevamot], according to both Rav and Shmuel, [the child] is forbidden to [marry] a Jewish woman [of valid lineage], for the shetuki that is stated according to Shmuel means that he is forbidden to [marry] a Jewish woman according to all the versions in the last chapter of Kiddushin; and according to the version of "examining" [the mother] it is even more difficult, for it implies that even through examining the mother, [the child] is only rendered fit according to Rabban Gamliel, but according to Rabbi Yehoshua, no — whereas here [Rav Yosef] says, "for he admits [it]," and [thus the child] is fit according to everyone! Perhaps one can distinguish: "having relations" there [in Yevamot/Kiddushin] means that he had relations with her one time, whereas "admitting" here — where it says "from him" — means that he had relations with her many times and was regularly with her constantly, as we say: "Most acts of intercourse follow the husband."

Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:9:1.hebrew: השבתנו על המעוברת - פי': לדידן ניחא, דאשה מזנה בודקת ומזנה ולא דמיא לשבויה; אלא לדידך דלית לך הך סברא — תינח מעוברת, אבל מדברת, אפילו לפי דבריך יש הפרש, דלזו יש עדים ולזו אין עדים ואיכא מיגו. אמר להם: מדברת היינו שבויה, וכמו ששבויה אין נאמנת לומר "לא נבעלתי", ה"נ מדברת, כדמסיק: לפי שאין אפוטרופוס לעריות. ומיהו פי' זה לא יתכן למאי דפרישית לעיל, דלר' יהושע נאמנת לומר "לא נבעלתי". ופר"י בדוחק: "מדברת היינו שבויה" — דכמו ששבויה בחזקת בעולה, כך מדברת בחזקת בעולה, לענין שאם אמרה "לכשר נבעלתי", שאינה נאמנת במיגו, לפי שיראה לומר "לא נבעלתי"; ולהכי אהני דאין אפוטרופוס לעריות, דלא חשבינן ליה מיגו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 13b:9:1.english: You answered us concerning the pregnant woman - Explanation: According to us [the Sages], it is understandable, for a promiscuous woman checks [i.e., takes precautions against pregnancy] and [then] engages in promiscuity, and [thus a pregnant woman] is not comparable to a captive. Rather, according to you [Rabbi Yehoshua], who do not hold this reasoning, it is well [regarding] a pregnant woman; but [regarding] a [woman seen] speaking [with a man], even according to your words there is a distinction, for this one [the captive] has witnesses [to her capture], whereas this one [the speaking woman] has no witnesses, and there is a miggo [that she could have claimed she did not have intercourse]. He said to them: [The case of] speaking is the same as [the case of] a captive — just as a captive is not believed to say, "I did not have intercourse," so too [the woman seen] speaking [is not believed], as [the Gemara] concludes: because there is no guardian for sexual immorality. However, this explanation is not tenable according to what I explained above, that according to Rabbi Yehoshua she is believed to say, "I did not have intercourse." And the Ri explained with difficulty: "[The case of] speaking is the same as [the case of] a captive" — just as a captive is in the presumptive status of having had intercourse, so too [the woman seen] speaking is in the presumptive status of having had intercourse, regarding [the law] that if she says, "I had intercourse with a fit man," she is not believed with a miggo, because she is afraid to say, "I did not have intercourse"; and for this [purpose], [the principle] that there is no guardian for sexual immorality is effective, [namely,] that we do not consider it a [valid] miggo.
